events.description: Every year an event comes along that tests mental and physical strengths of its racers like no other. Pisgah Productions proudly presents the hardest (and most fun) thing you will do this year….. the DOUBLE DARE. Teams of two riders will race to reach up to 10 checkpoints (CPs) per day, two days in a row. The race begins at 10AM on Saturday and every team must be back before 10PM. The race resumes at 6AM Sunday with 10 brand new checkpoints. Every team must finish before 6PM on Sunday. Teams ‘in the running’ should expect up to 70 miles of riding with 12,000-15,000 feet of climbing each day. SINGLE-DARE! The one-day category at Double-Dare!!! events.title: GTC Paris Mountain Road Race
events.description: General Race Information The Paris Mountain Road Race 10k is a hilly run around the base of Paris Mountain starting and finishing at Redeemer Presbyterian Church at 6150 Old Buncombe Rd., Greenville, SC. The total elevation gain over the 10K distance is roughly 1500 feet. With over 2500 vertical feet of elevation gain, 89 curves, and some hills at 15% grade, the Paris Mountain Road Race 20k lives up to its billing as the TOUGHEST RACE IN THE SOUTH. The race starts at Redeemer Presbyterian Church, ascends the north side of Paris Mountain, descends on the south side, and uses the hilly back roads at the base of the mountain to return. Sorry, but strollers and dogs are not permitted in the Paris Mountain Road Races.

events.title: Conquer the Rock 25k & 50k
events.description: 🏞️ Welcome to the Mountain’s Challenge So, you wish to walk among the clouds? ☁️ Then lace up, for this journey takes you over the mighty backs of Pinnacle Mountain and the legendary Table Rock, two of South Carolina’s tallest guardians of stone. 🗻 These trails? events.description: The Bootlegger is one of the most challenging and scenic gravel events of the year! There are two route choices (58 and 85 miles) that both start and finish in downtown Lenoir, NC and travel through the beautiful and rugged Wilson Creek Gorge. The 58 mile route has approximately 4500 feet of climbing while the 85 includes approximately 7250 feet of climbing. Be sure to keep your head up and enjoy the scenery as the Bootlegger 100 takes you from historic downtown Lenoir and into the heart of the “other Pisgah,” also known as the Grandfather Ranger District. Both the 85 and 58 mile options roll through the countryside before delivering you to a gravel wonderland with plenty of challenging terrain. events.title: Pisgah Mountain Bike Adventure Race
events.description: The Pisgah Mountain Bike Adventure Race (PMBAR) is the absolute pinnacle of MTB Adventure Racing. A mix of brutal and beautiful, this test of spirit and camaraderie tasks teams of two racers to reach 4 of 5 checkpoints, in any order, and return to the start/finish as fast as possible. The team with the lowest overall time wins. Checkpoint locations remain secret until start-time and there is no suggested route. Routes vary between 50-80 miles, include 9,000-15,000 feet of climbing, and take 7-14 hours to complete. PMBAR is held deep in the Pisgah National Forest, one of the most beautiful, rugged, and unforgiving areas in the nation. There will be little to no water or food support on course. events.title: Biltmore Kiwanis Classic
events.description: Join us for the 27th running of the Biltmore Classic. Choose from the 5k or 15k distances. This race deserves to be on every runners bucket-list and will indeed be on every runners “best race” list. Nestled in the blue ridge mountains, the Biltmore Estate was built for George Washington Vanderbilt II between 1889 and 1895 and holds the record of being the largest privately owned house in the United States. The Biltmore-Kiwanis Classic 15k and 5k races have been running on the estate since 1997 and act as the biggest fundraiser for Asheville’s Kiwanis Club.

events.title: GTC Upville Mile
events.description: Why run down when you can run up ? GTC Upville Mile is a 1-mile, uphill-only road race in Paris Mountain State Park, on the steepest part of Paris Mountain State Park Road. The route is one of the toughest, if not the toughest uphill 1-mile road segments in the Upstate, including nearby Altamont Road, and the road going up Sassafras Mountain. If you like a running challenge, this event may be just the ticket for you. Don't be surprised though if you find it necessary to do at least a couple short walk breaks. It's recommended you practice on this route before you race on it. With an average grade of 8.2%, and elevation gain of 460 feet in just a mile, it surely will not disappoint. John Hart, Race Director
